10. Rounding rules

we have this in traffic/billing.py and I think we should settle on this if we can. Perhaps it belongs in traffic/utilities?

def calculate_amount(quantity, unit_price):
    """
    Calculate an invoice amount in integer cents.

    quantity may be fractional.
    unit_price is integer cents.
    """

    if quantity is None or unit_price is None:
        return 0

    return int(
        (
            Decimal(str(quantity))
            * Decimal(unit_price)
        ).quantize(
            Decimal("1"),
            rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP
        )
    )

One thing I can already say from your grep

This is significant:

taxable_subtotal INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
tax INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0

and:

taxable INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1
tax_rate INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0

with the comment:

    -- Tax rate stored in basis points:

So there is already a design for tax at both invoice and invoice-item levels.

That directly contradicts my earlier statement that there was "currently no tax system in the billing schema." I was wrong.

And this is particularly interesting because your note from earlier today was:

    "tax info for the invoice detail line is not showing or editable."

The schema appears to have precisely the data needed for that:

invoice_items
    taxable
    tax_rate

So we may not need to invent a tax design at all. We may instead need to finish implementing the design that we already started.

Let's look at those three outputs before we make another decision.

How is it that you forget this and what can I do on my end to alleviate this problem?

You're right to be frustrated. The short answer is: I don't have a reliable, complete transcript of every prior project conversation available as working context. I can have summaries, memories, and portions of the current/project conversation, but those are not equivalent to having the entire history searchable at every moment.

In this case, the failure was worse than simply "forgetting." I made a factual claim without verifying it against the files you were working from. Your grep immediately demonstrated that the schema already contained the tax model. I should have searched first.
What you can do on your end

The most useful thing is actually what you just did: keep the project notes/files authoritative and have me inspect them rather than relying on conversational memory.

For a project like zbTraffic, I'd suggest:

    Keep a short design-decisions document in the repo.
    Something like:

    docs/design_decisions.md

    with decisions such as:

        monetary values are integer cents

        invoice is generated only from completed spots

        Draft invoices have no invoice number

        PREPAID → CLEARED after payment requirement is satisfied

        etc.

    When we make an important architectural decision, put it in that document.
    It doesn't need to be formal. A dated bullet is enough.

    At the beginning of a new work session, have me read the relevant design notes before changing code.
    That's much more reliable than asking me to remember what we decided three days ago.

    For schema questions, have me inspect create_database.py before I make claims about the schema.
    Your current example is exactly why. The source code is the authority.

    Keep the prototype/backups clearly distinguished from production/business logic.
    We've now discovered another source of confusion: the throwaway GUI can permit states that the intended application won't. That makes interpreting its behavior dangerous.

And something I can do better

I should adopt a stronger rule for this project:

    When we're making a design decision, distinguish between what I remember, what I infer, and what I have verified in the current source.

If I don't have the source in front of me, I should say:

    "I don't know; let's inspect it."

rather than filling the gap from memory.

That's particularly important for schema, business rules, and previously agreed architectural decisions. Those are areas where a confident-but-wrong answer can send us in circles, exactly as you described earlier.

And I think your grep exercise has already shown us the right way forward. The repository is the source of truth; our conversation is the record of why we made the decisions. When those conflict, we should stop and investigate rather than assume.

For this morning's billing work, I would therefore treat the current source tree + your recovered notes from last night as authoritative, and use my conversational memory only as a guide to what we should look for.

======================================================================

Aug 28/2026
Tax rates
---------
For the initial implementation, zbTraffic supports one applicable
sales-tax rate at a time.

tax_rates:
    id
    name
    rate
    effective_date

Rate is stored as integer basis points.

The applicable rate is determined from effective_date.

Separate city/state/local tax rates are not supported initially.

Customer tax_status determines whether the customer is TAXABLE
or EXEMPT.
